crossRefs.note: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man will perish,
that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?
I have seen the wicked in great power, spreading himself like a green tree in its native soil.
But he passed away, and behold, he was not. Yes, I sought him, but he could not be found.
He followed her immediately, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a fool stepping into a noose.
Until an arrow strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and doesn’t know that it will cost his life.
Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
“So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day…
For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.
For when they are saying, “Peace and safety,” then sudden destruction will come on them, like birth pains on a pregnant…

people.name: Esther
people.line: Jewish queen of Persia; saved her people from genocide.

people.name: Haman
people.line: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.

translations.web: Haman also said, “Yes, Esther the queen let no man come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I am also invited by her together with the king.
translations.bsb: “What is more,” Haman added, “Queen Esther invited no one but me to join the king at the banquet she prepared, and I am invited back tomorrow along with the king.
translations.kjv: Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no man come in with the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to morrow am I invited unto her also with the king.
translations.asv: Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no man come in with the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to-morrow also am I invited by her together with the king.
